waypoints.title: Star Formation in the Galaxy
waypoints.description: Colloquium version. Thesis: environment shapes the outcome of star formation, and the environments that matter most for cosmic star formation are the dense ones — not the nearby low-mass clouds where our intuition was built. Star formation sets the luminosity, chemistry, and dynamics of galaxies; a 100 Msun star outshines a 1 Msun star by ~10^6, so the high-mass end of the IMF dominates the observables even though it contributes little of the mass. The question throughout: is the IMF universal, and if not, what sets it?

waypoints.title: The Local Benchmark
waypoints.description: Our detailed picture of star formation comes from Taurus (~140 pc), Perseus, and Orion (~400 pc). These clouds produce almost exclusively low-mass stars, have low volume densities, and form few bound clusters: only ~5-10% of stars locally end up in bound clusters. Extrapolating from this sample to the conditions that produced most of the Universe's stars is an extrapolation of several orders of magnitude in density and pressure.

waypoints.title: Orion: The Resolved Limit
waypoints.description: The ONC is the nearest high-mass star-forming region and our only chance to resolve individual protostellar disks around massive YSOs. Orion Source I, embedded behind this nebula, is the closest high-mass protostar and the object where the salt-bearing disk phenomenon was first characterized. We return to it later.

waypoints.title: The CMZ: A z~2 Analog In Reach
waypoints.description: ~10^8 Msun of molecular gas within ~200 pc, producing ~10% of the Galaxy's star formation. Gas densities, pressures, turbulent line widths, temperatures, and cosmic-ray rates all exceed local values by 1-3 orders of magnitude. The Kruijssen (2012) cluster formation efficiency framework predicts CFE > 30% at these densities versus 5-10% locally; Ginsburg & Kruijssen (2018) found that Sgr B2 is consistent with the high-CFE prediction. These conditions resemble the z~2 peak of the cosmic SFR density, at 8 kpc instead of Gpc.

waypoints.title: ACES: The Complete Millimeter Census
waypoints.description: The ALMA CMZ Exploration Survey covers the whole CMZ at 2.4 arcsec resolution — versus ~15 arcsec for the previous best complete maps — in continuum and ~25 spectral lines, combining 12m, 7m, and total power data. Shown: ACES 3mm continuum feathered with the GBT/MUSTANG-2 90 GHz map, so structures from 2 arcsec to degrees are recovered simultaneously. Combined with existing radio and infrared surveys, the CMZ is now mapped continuously from ~2 micron to 10 cm.

waypoints.title: HNCO: Dense Gas and Shocks
waypoints.description: Integrated intensity of HNCO 4(0,4)-3(0,3), masked at high significance. HNCO traces dense gas and is enhanced in mildly shocked material, so it picks out both the cloud population and the shear-driven structures along the CMZ orbital streams. Line maps like this one are the primary product of ACES: continuum tells you where the mass is, lines tell you its temperature, density, kinematics, and chemistry.

waypoints.title: SiO 2-1: The Shock Tracer
waypoints.description: SiO requires grain sputtering to release Si into the gas phase, so it is nearly absent in quiescent gas and bright in fast shocks. In the CMZ it traces cloud-cloud collisions, protostellar outflows, and supernova-driven compression. Comparing SiO morphology against HNCO and the continuum separates dynamically active gas from gas that is merely dense.

waypoints.title: H40-alpha: The Ionized Census
waypoints.description: The H40-alpha recombination line gives an extinction-free measure of ionized gas, i.e. of the already-formed OB population, and it is kinematically resolved — unlike free-free continuum. This is how we tie the current star formation rate to the embedded protostellar population traced by the dust continuum, in a single dataset with a single calibration.

waypoints.title: M0.8-0.2: A Supernova-Blown Shell
waypoints.description: An early ACES result: a ~20 pc molecular ring whose morphology and kinematics are consistent with a supernova expanding into a dense cloud. It matters because it is a concrete instance of the feedback term that regulates star formation in the CMZ, and because the same explosion both disrupts the cloud and compresses parts of it. Whether such events are net-positive or net-negative for star formation is not yet settled.

waypoints.title: The MUBLO
waypoints.description: G0.02467-0.0727: a compact millimeter source with line widths of several hundred km/s in multiple species, no infrared counterpart, no X-ray counterpart, and no radio jet. Candidate interpretations include an intermediate-mass black hole accretion event, a stellar merger remnant, or an extreme evolved-star/protostellar object. None fits cleanly. Follow-up is ongoing; it is included here as an example of what a complete unbiased survey turns up.

waypoints.title: Sgr B2: 50-80% of CMZ Star Formation
waypoints.description: ~10^7 Msun in a single cloud, hosting two clusters of >10^4 Msun each within <3 pc, and responsible for the majority of ongoing star formation in the CMZ. Accretion along the large-scale filaments feeding the cloud runs at ~0.1 Msun/yr. If you want to test cluster formation theory against a system that is actually forming a young massive cluster, this is the nearest laboratory.

waypoints.title: Sgr B2 With JWST: Asymmetric Star Formation
waypoints.description: JWST imaging of Sgr B2 reveals a sharp spatial boundary in the distribution of young stars: one side of the cloud is actively forming stars, the other is not, with a transition far sharper than any smooth density gradient would produce. The natural reading is a large-scale compression event propagating through the cloud. The southern portion of the cloud, Sgr B2 Deep South, hosts a distributed population of protostellar sources well away from the classic N and M cores.

waypoints.title: Sgr B2 N: Cores at 1mm
waypoints.description: At ~1mm the emission is a mixture of protostellar dust cores and optically thick free-free from hypercompact HII regions; separating the two requires multi-frequency continuum fitting. Budaiev et al. (2024) cataloged the protostellar core population in N and M. The core mass function here is measured in the densest star-forming environment available, which makes it the strongest test of environmental variation in the CMF.

waypoints.title: Fragmentation in Sgr B2
waypoints.description: Resolved into individual YSOs, Sgr B2's 'cores' break down as roughly 17% starless, 37% single-YSO, 45% multiple — noting that the physical scale sampled here is larger than in the nearby ALMA-IMF fields, so this comparison must be done at matched linear resolution. The trend across all samples: more massive cores fragment more, but the mass stays concentrated in the dominant fragment. Massive cores make massive stars and companions, not many equal-mass stars.

waypoints.title: Hot Cores and the Jeans Mass
waypoints.description: Hot cores — T > 100 K, chemically rich, ice-sublimated — mark active high-mass accretion. Jeff et al. (2024) measured the thermal structure of 15+ hot cores in Sgr B2 DS. The consequence matters for the IMF: M_J scales as T^(3/2) rho^(-1/2), so the elevated temperatures in a hot-core-rich protocluster raise the Jeans mass by factors of 5-10 over the surrounding gas. Heating suppresses fragmentation into low-mass objects and channels residual gas onto the most massive sinks.

waypoints.title: ALMA-IMF: The Protocluster Sample
waypoints.description: 15 high-mass protoclusters at 2-6 kpc, observed in ALMA Bands 3 and 6, spanning young/quiescent to evolved/feedback-dominated. The design goal is a core mass function measured uniformly across evolutionary stage at ~2000 au resolution. W51, shown here in JWST imaging, contributes two of the most active fields: W51-E and W51-IRS2.

waypoints.title: W51-IRS2 at 3mm
waypoints.description: ALMA 3mm continuum of W51-IRS2. Roughly 1000 cores are now cataloged across the ALMA-IMF sample, with masses from ~1.6 to ~200 Msun. The measured CMF is steeper than the raw core counts naively suggest but remains shallower than the Salpeter/Chabrier IMF slope, and shallower than CMFs measured in low-mass clouds. A top-heavy CMF in high-mass protoclusters is the central observational claim.

waypoints.title: W51-E: Core-to-Star Conversion
waypoints.description: Resolving cores into YSOs is what converts a CMF into an IMF prediction. W51-E: ~25% starless, ~30% single YSO, ~45% multiple. W51-IRS2: ~53% starless, ~39% single, ~8% multiple. The two fields differ mainly in evolutionary state, which is exactly the systematic that a single-epoch CMF measurement cannot control for.

waypoints.title: The JWST-ALMA Disconnect
waypoints.description: Same region, JWST NIRCam. In W51, only ~10% of sources are detected by both JWST and ALMA. JWST picks up later-stage YSOs whose envelopes have been depleted; ALMA picks up the deeply embedded population. The envelope-rich, infrared-invisible phase is therefore short and luminous. Any YSO count — and any star formation rate derived from one — has to be interpreted stage by stage, or the two telescopes will disagree by an order of magnitude for reasons that have nothing to do with the physics.

waypoints.title: Chaotic Accretion in W51 North
waypoints.description: The W51 North outflow has changed direction by ~50 degrees in less than 100 years, while ~0.25-0.5 Msun was accreted. That requires a disk whose angular momentum axis is being reset on a dynamical timescale — episodic, misaligned infall rather than a steady disk. If reorientation events of this magnitude are common, the accretion history that sets a massive star's final mass is far less smooth than parametric models assume.

waypoints.title: No Massive Starless Cores
waypoints.description: ALMA-IMF, ALMA-ATOMS, and ALMAGAL all fail to find massive starless cores in any significant number. Massive stars therefore do not begin life inside massive reservoirs that are already assembled; they start from ordinary-mass seeds and keep accreting from a replenished supply. This favors competitive/clump-fed accretion over turbulent-core models, and it means the CMF is a snapshot of an evolving distribution, not an initial condition.

waypoints.title: Hot Cores as an Accretion Diagnostic
waypoints.description: 76 hot cores were identified across ALMA-IMF via methyl formate emission; roughly 10% of massive continuum cores sit inside one. Working hypothesis, supported by the samples in W51, Sgr B2, and the ALMA-IMF fields: every high-mass YSO passes through a hot-core phase while accreting. That makes complex-organic emission a selection tool for actively accreting massive protostars, and it makes the associated heating a systematic, not an accident.

waypoints.title: Salts in Disks
waypoints.description: Gas-phase NaCl and KCl, previously seen only in AGB envelopes, are now detected in ~9 high-mass YSO disks including Orion Source I. Salt correlates with H2O, SiS, and PN, and anti-correlates with COMs and ionized gas — it selects a distinct disk component. Its practical value: the salt lines are optically thin, spatially compact, and Keplerian, giving a direct dynamical mass. For Orion Source I that yields ~15 Msun.

waypoints.title: The Salt Excitation Problem
waypoints.description: Vibrational temperatures of ~1000 K coexist with rotational temperatures of ~50-150 K in the same salt-bearing gas. That is far from LTE and requires radiative pumping by an intense, non-blackbody field, plausibly in the 25-40 micron range. Two open questions: what produces that radiation field, and why is salt present in only a subset of otherwise similar disks?

waypoints.title: The Brick: Dense, Quiescent, Instructive
waypoints.description: G0.253+0.016 holds ~10^5 Msun at densities that would guarantee vigorous star formation locally, yet forms almost nothing. It is the control case for the CMZ: same environment, opposite outcome from Sgr B2. Explanations invoke high turbulent pressure, strong magnetic support, an early evolutionary state, or a raised effective Jeans mass from elevated temperatures — these are separable with the right observations.

waypoints.title: Ice Mapping With Narrowband JWST
waypoints.description: F466N is sensitive to CO ice, the XCN feature, and H2O; F405N provides the nearby continuum reference. Differencing them turns background stars into thousands of independent absorption probes through the cloud. The observed anticorrelation between color and extinction is driven by ice absorption reaching >2 magnitudes — a per-sightline ice column, not a stacked average.

waypoints.title: Ice Abundances and Metallicity
waypoints.description: Local clouds give roughly 3:1:1 for H2O:CO:CO2 ice. In the Brick, CO ice abundance rises with column density and the CO fraction is higher than the local benchmark, implying colder and better-shielded interiors than the temperature measurements alone suggest. The larger prize: ice column ratios measured photometrically are a metallicity probe in regions where optical spectroscopy is impossible — the approach SPHEREx will apply across the sky.

waypoints.title: Sgr C: The Other Extreme
waypoints.description: Sgr C has a comparable dense gas reservoir to Sgr B2 but a far lower star formation rate, and it sits at the opposite end of the CMZ. The pair defines the dynamic range that any model of CMZ star formation has to reproduce: an order-of-magnitude spread in efficiency at fixed large-scale environment. Orbital phase, shear, and collision history are the leading candidate discriminants.

waypoints.title: Arches and Quintuplet: The End State
waypoints.description: Two ~10^4 Msun clusters, a few Myr old, already gas-free. Their IMFs have been repeatedly reported as top-heavy, with all the usual caveats about mass segregation, incompleteness, and differential extinction. They are the endpoint of the process we watch in Sgr B2, and the consistency check on any claim of a varying IMF: whatever the CMF does at 2000 au must be reconcilable with what these clusters look like at 3 Myr.

waypoints.title: Feedback in Action
waypoints.description: The Sickle traces the interaction of the Quintuplet's radiation field with the surrounding molecular gas. Feedback enters the star formation rate equation twice — as the term that terminates accretion onto individual protostars, and as the term that disperses or compresses the remaining cloud. In the CMZ both act on timescales comparable to the orbital time, which is why the CMZ's star formation rate is variable rather than steady.

waypoints.title: NGC 6334: The Disk-Scale Comparison
waypoints.description: One of the ALMA-IMF fields, and a nearby template for what the CMZ protoclusters would look like at higher resolution and lower extinction. Building matched-resolution, matched-tracer samples across a range of environments is the only way to isolate the environmental dependence from the resolution and evolutionary-stage systematics that dominate literature comparisons.

waypoints.title: Westerlund 2: Feedback-Sculpted Remnants
waypoints.description: A young massive cluster that has already cleared its natal gas, leaving photoevaporating globules with tails pointing away from the ionizing sources. These are the objects where the competition between compression-triggered collapse and radiative destruction is directly visible, at the scale where disks and low-mass stars are made or unmade.

waypoints.title: Synthesis: Cooperative Accretion
waypoints.description: Assembling the pieces: no massive starless cores, so massive stars grow from ordinary seeds by continued accretion. Every accreting massive YSO makes a hot core, so protoclusters are heated from within by many sources at once. Elevated T raises M_J by 5-10x, suppressing fragmentation into low-mass objects. Gas that would have made low-mass stars instead flows onto the dominant sinks. The prediction is a top-heavy IMF in dense protoclusters — which is what the CMF measurements and the CMZ cluster IMFs both point toward.

waypoints.title: Open Questions
waypoints.description: 1. Does the CMF-to-IMF mapping vary with environment, or does fragmentation cancel the top-heavy CMF? 2. How often do accretion-terminating dynamical events like the W51 North reorientation occur, and do they set the upper mass cutoff? 3. Why is salt present in only some disks, and what pumps the vibrational levels? 4. Is the fragmentation-versus-core-mass trend physical or a resolution-and-sensitivity artifact? 5. Can ice photometry deliver metallicities precisely enough to be competitive?

waypoints.title: Explore the Data
waypoints.description: All layers shown are real survey data: ACES (ALMA 12m/7m/TP + GBT MUSTANG-2), ALMA-IMF, JWST NIRCam/MIRI/NIRISS, MeerKAT, Spitzer, Hubble, Gemini. Pan, zoom, and use the layer control to compare tracers at any position. The waypoint menu jumps to any stop and the link button copies a deep link to it. A general-audience version of this tour, and single-region wavelength explorers for the Brick, Sgr B2, W51, and the Sickle, are on the index page.
